title: Calendar features known in advance
note: A target day's weekday, season and German public holiday status are known ahead of time, so they're safe to use at any horizon. Bridge days (a working day next to a holiday) and Christmas week get their own flags because many people take them off.

title: Origin-relative rows: the anti-leakage core
note: For every (origin, horizon) pair, lags are read at integer positions ≤ the origin's position i. The same-weekday mean walks back from the origin, and the year-ago value is used only if it's already observed (j ≤ i). A 14-day-ahead row sees exactly what a forecaster would know at that moment.

title: Baselines worth beating
note: Seasonal naive repeats last week. Holt-Winters (damped additive trend, additive weekly seasonality) is refit at every backtest origin on the last 3 years. MASE divides MAE by the seasonal-naive in-sample error, so MASE < 1 means beating 'same day last week'.

title: Conformal bands per horizon
note: A model trained only to 2015 is backtested on 2016. Its absolute residuals, grouped by horizon, give band half-widths that widen with distance into the future. The final model (trained to 2016) reuses those widths, and 2017 checks whether the stated coverage holds.

title: Rolling-origin backtest
note: 51 Sunday origins in 2017, each forecasting 14 days. Holt-Winters is refit per origin; the GBM is fixed but reads fresh lags at every origin. Metrics are then cut by horizon and by holiday to find where each model breaks.

title: Serving a forecast
note: The API builds the same origin-relative rows with the same function used in training (no train/serve skew), runs all three models, and returns horizon-specific bands plus 8 weeks of history for context.
